summary: A very common fungal leaf disease. Target-like spots start on older leaves; severe cases reduce tuber size.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern) on older leaves
Spots enlarge and leaves die from the bottom up
key_sign: Brown spots with concentric rings, starting on the lowest, oldest leaves.
favourable_conditions: Warm weather with alternating wet and dry periods; stressed or ageing plants are more susceptible.
spread: Survives in infected plant debris and soil; spores spread by wind and rain splash.

today: Remove the most heavily spotted lower leaves
this_week: Apply a protectant fungicide registered for early blight if spots are spreading
Keep plants well fed: nitrogen-stressed plants get worse early blight
next_two_weeks: Keep monitoring; separate from late blight, which spreads much faster

chemical: Protectants such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil; systemic options such as azoxystrobin or difenoconazole as registered
cultural: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for at least 2 years

prevention: Maintain good fertility and irrigation to reduce plant stress

summary: The disease behind the Irish potato famine. In cool, wet weather it can destroy a field within days and rot tubers in storage.
symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches that spread rapidly, often with a pale green or yellow border
White, downy growth on the leaf underside in humid conditions
Brown lesions on stems; reddish-brown dry rot in tubers
key_sign: Fast-spreading, water-soaked dark patches with white fuzz underneath in humid weather.
favourable_conditions: Cool nights, mild days and long periods of leaf wetness (rain, fog, heavy dew).
spread: Spores travel long distances on wind and rain; survives in infected seed tubers, cull piles and volunteer plants.

today: Remove and bag infected plants; do not compost them
Warn neighbouring potato and tomato growers: late blight is a community disease
this_week: Apply a fungicide registered for late blight to the whole field immediately, then at short label intervals while weather stays wet
Ask your agriculture officer to confirm and advise on fungicide choice
next_two_weeks: Kill vines completely 2-3 weeks before harvest so tubers are not infected
Harvest in dry weather and do not store damaged tubers

chemical: Protectants such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil, plus late-blight-specific products such as cyazofamid, mandipropamid or cymoxanil combinations, as registered; rotate groups
cultural: Destroy cull piles and volunteer potatoes
Hill soil over tubers to protect them from spores

summary: No disease signs were found on this potato leaf.
key_sign: Uniform green leaf with no spots.

this_week: Inspect a few plants, including leaf undersides
next_two_weeks: Keep monitoring, especially after rain or humid spells

prevention: Rotate away from potato and tomato
Scout more often in cool, wet weather
